pass_a_gloss: —and toward contemplation the appetite seems to be hunger and thirst as things that produce psychic health: if ever the enemy should thirst with such hunger or thirst after repenting of what he sinned, the holy person must give him the holy bread when he hungers, if he is not a dog or pig unworthy of the holy things. And in many ways one can feed a hungering enemy—sometimes by a teaching word, sometimes by prayer concerning him. And since the head of every man is Christ, therefore of the enemy, as not being a man because of impiety, the head is the antichrist, whom one must make vanish as opposed to the Word of God by the coals of the rational fire, whenever the impious one who has the antichrist as head, having hungered, eats—
pass_b_english: —and the appetite for contemplation seems to be hunger and thirst, as things that work health in the soul. If the enemy ever feels that hunger or thirst after repenting of his sins, the holy person must give him the holy bread when he hungers—unless he is a dog or pig unworthy of holy things.

There are many ways to feed a hungry enemy: sometimes by a teaching word, sometimes by prayer for him. And since [[the head of every man is Christ >> Bible:1 Corinthians 11:3]], the enemy—as not a 'man' because of impiety—has the antichrist as head. That head must be consumed as opposed to the Word of God by the coals of rational fire, whenever the impious one whose head is the antichrist, hungering, eats—

choices.choice: Read as hunger for virtue and contemplation after repentance, not only bodily need.
Kept Origen's Christ/antichrist head contrast tight to 1 Cor 11:3.
